title: Variant Pathways: Enterprise Intake, Pinning, and Deprecation Playbook
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable triage and pathing playbook for enterprise model onboarding requests that involve model variant choices (e.g., base vs quantized, adapter vs full model), explicit version pinning, and planned deprecations. Focus is on balancing enterprise SLAs (stability/pinning) with platform economics (encouraging compatible fallbacks and graceful offramps).

Scope: New model submissions; requests to pin customers to specific versions; scheduled deprecation announcements; and the eval gate matrix required for enterprise acceptance. Excludes production incident response, which is handled via reliability runbooks.

Outcomes: a) A triage rubric that surface-prioritizes enterprise requests with data sensitivity or SLA needs; b) A documented pathway for variant mapping (compatibility table + recommended fallback variants); c) Standardized pinning policy with retention windows and rollback criteria; d) Deprecation cadence and customer communication templates; e) Clear eval gate checklist (functionality, hallucination, latency/cost regression thresholds).
acceptance_criteria: Triage rubric implemented in intake form and validated with 5 enterprise requests during the pilot
Variant compatibility mapping template published to Confluence and linked from catalog UI
Pinning policy approved by Legal & Security and added to onboarding checklist
Deprecation playbook includes automated customer notification path and migration plan templates
Eval gate defined with pass/fail thresholds for accuracy (ROUGE-like), hallucination spot checks, latency P95, and token-cost delta

decisions: Decision 1: Default enterprise pin window = 90 days (string), with explicit contract-based extensions. Rationale: limits long-term fragmentation while meeting most enterprise stability needs.
Decision 2: Require 'compatibility probe' (ENG-20455) for any quantized/adapter variant before catalog listing. Rationale: avoid silent runtime fallbacks that break SLAs.

Decision 3: Deprecation minimum notice = 60 days for non-security deprecations, 7 days for critical security/bugfix-only deprecations. Rationale: balance customer migration time vs. patch cycle urgency.
Decision 4: Pilot will treat 'enterprise-sensitivity' flag as top-tier priority in intake, triggering manual review by Solutions Engineering within 48 hours.
tradeoffs: Allowing long-term pinning increases operational cost and model fragmentation, but reduces enterprise churn for regulated customers.
Tight eval thresholds reduce regression risk but may slow onboarding time and raise initial friction for new open-source model variants.
Automating compatibility checks speeds catalog throughput but requires engineering investment (ENG-20455).
risks: High risk of version proliferation if pinning is too permissive—could double caching and GPU footprint for enterprise tenants.
Customer friction if deprecation notices are insufficiently actionable (missing migration steps).
Security/compliance risk for private deployments if onboarding skips KMS/HSM verification for pinned variants.
mitigations: Introduce per-tenant pin quotas (default 3 pinned versions) and charge for additional pins via billing/contract terms.
Ship migration helper scripts and sample prompts for common migration paths between variants (e.g., full -> quantized) in the catalog docs.
Make KMS/HSM checks mandatory for private enterprise variant acceptances; integrate with onboarding checklist.

Number of active pins per tenant (target <= 3 default)
Post-onboarding regression rate measured by eval gate failures within 14 days (target < 10%)
Customer satisfaction NPS for onboarding (target >= 60 for pilot customers)
Catalog fragmentation metric: number of live incompatible variants (target reduce 30% vs baseline)
